OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Administrative
Violation Date: 5/15/2023
Violation Code: OGA3211(G) - WELL PERMITS - POSTING - Failure to post the well permit number and the operator's name, address and phone number at the well site during construction of the access road, site preparation and during drilling, operating or alteration of well.
Violation ID: 995071
Permit API: 053-29573
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/15/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack. Neither the well operator or permit number is posted on the well or well site.This well is plumbed into a 2000 gallon plastic tank located next to the well. The upper portion of this tank is cracked/broken. This tank is approximately one-third full with production fluid from the well, including crude oil. There is no containment in place around this tank.The specific conductance (SPC) of the soil in the proximity of the valve for this tank and a smaller tote adjacent to the tank is elevated. In addition to elevated SPC, the soil is stained, vegetation is stressed and deer tracks are abundant near the tank and tote. The SPC of standing water and soil in the roadside ditch that runs next to the tank is also elevated for approximately 200 feet both to the north and south of the tank.The access road between this well and 053-29570 has not been properly maintained. As a result, the installed BMPs are not functional and accelerated erosion of the road surface has occurred. Numerous other sections of lease roads throughout the Warrant 2878 lease have also been neglected and are in need of repair/maintenance to be considered in compliance.Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material at this well site.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 5/09/2023 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Bell Twp, Clearfield county. 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/09/2023
Violation Code: 78.66(b) - REPORTING RELEASES - Owner or operator failed to report a reportable release of brine on or into the ground at the well site within 2 hours after detecting or discovering the releases.
Violation ID: 994405
Permit API: 033-23623
Unconventional: No
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Bell Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/09/2023
Comments: Routine site inspection at conventional well 033-23623 on May 9, 2023. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. No combustible or methane gases were detected.Exposed soil and dead vegetation was observed downslope of the production equipment. The exposed soil was inundated with deer tracks. I screened the area for conductivity using a Hanna soil probe. Elevated soil readings were observed ranging from 1.0 mS/cm to 3.75 mS/cm. I collected a soil sample (3442-664). The sample was sent to the Departments lab in Harrisburg and will be analyzed for SAC 530 plus, bromide, lithium, and strontium. The Department recommends that the operator address the remediation of the brine release in accordance with small spill policy 800-5000-001. Violations have been cited.

Inspection Date: 7/27/2023
Comments: On July 27 2023, the Department conducted a follow up inspection in response to IR 3491397,3387914, 3514511 and 3543627. Accompanying into today's inspection was the landowner. The findings were as follows: According to the Order issued to the operator by the Department for this site, the Operator shall completely restore the well site within 9 months after plugging. The well site and access road are not restored during today's inspection, not exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. According to the landowner, the site has not been restored to pre-existing contours.The well was plugged on October 7, 2021 according the the plugging certificate submitted by the Operator for this well. As such, the Operator was to completely restore the well site no later than July 7, 2022. E and S Plan has not been received by the Department as previously requested in IRs 3262679, 3387914, 3514511 and 3543627. No E and S Plan was found on site. Lack of adequate uniform vegetation is still observed due to multiple areas of exposed soil and rock. There are several bare spots throughout the former well site that are lacking adequate uniform vegetation. No E and S BMPs are installed on site. The ground appears to be seeded in most areas, but 70% uniform vegetation has not been achieved at this time. Vegetative growth may be hindered by the amount of rock and gravel on site. The Department recommends the Operator take necessary measures to ensure 70% uniform vegetative growth is achieved for restoration of the site. Based on today's inspection, violations shall remain outstanding.The transmission of this inspection is delayed due to an IT error.

Report Details

Violation ID: 8181534
Permit API: 117-22231
Unconventional: Yes
County: Tioga

Inspection Date: 3/29/2024
Comments: On 3/29/2024, DEP representative John Rogers conducted an admin inspection for the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. This inspection is to report the results of two water samples that were collected during drilling operations from two different locations at the site.During inspection #3724668 conducted on 3/6/2024, the department discovered instances of elevated conductance fluid on the north side of the pad surface and in the sediment basin below the north side of the pad. On 3/27/2024, the department received the results of the samples. Sample 9551-087 was collected from a channel of water along the north perimeter berm that appeared to have a white substance along the length of it. The water field tested at 4.10 mS conductance. The puddle was near the outfall leading to the sediment basin and was approximately 60 feet long and ranged from 6 inches to 2 feet wide and up to 1.5 inches deep. A 2 inch wide by 1 inch deep stream of water was flowing down the outfall that field tested at 4.11 mS conductance. The water was flowing down to the northeast end of the sediment basin. The results are shown in pictures 1 and 2. Sample 9551-088 was collected from the sediment basin where a white plume was visible leading into the sediment basin coming from the rock outfall leading off the pad. The flow of water leading into the sediment basin from the pad field tested at 2.48 mS conductance. The results are shown in pictures 3 and 4.Noted during inspection #3724668, water leaving the sediment basin field tested at 1.156 mS conductance. Water flowing off location field tested at 1.084 mS conductance. During previous inspections, water flowing in a channel below the northeast corner of the pad and below the sediment basin field tested at 0.3 mS conductance or less.The samples show elevated levels of aluminum, iron, chlorides and strontium which indicates the release of a pollutional substance on the pad and reaching the basin.During inspection 3704886 conducted on 1/29/2023, sample 9551-080 was collected from a channel of water along the northeast cornerof the pad that field tested at 4.2 mS conductance. The laboratory analysis of the sample showed elevated levels of pH, calcium, iron, chlorides and strontium as shown in pictures 5 and 6. Bags of deicing media was reported as being applied near this area.The release of an unknown volume of elevated conductance fluid to the pad surface and into the sedimentation basin constitutes violations of SWMA 301, CSL 402, 25 PA Code 78a.56(a) and 78a.66(b)(2).This incident has the potential to cause pollution as defined by 25 PA Code 93.6(a), 25 PA Code 93.6(b), and 25 PA Code 91.33(a) and does not meet the discharge requirements under 25 PA Code 78a.60(b).Because of the large volume of elevated conductance fluid discovered on the pad surface and in the sedimentation basin, the DEP recommends pursuing Act 2. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3724668 for a 6' x 60' puddle of water with elevated conductance and with a white substance in it; discovered on the unprotected pad surface and flowing into the sediment basin during drilling operations.The DEP recommends the following: 1. The department recommends that Seneca determine the source of the white substance, elevated conductance, pH, aluminum, iron, and strontium in the water sample and take measures to address it, including but not limited to; ceasing discharge, collecting the water for reuse/disposal, etc.2. Assess the area of elevated conductance fluid at the north side of the pad and the basin; clean/report as necessary.

Comments: On March 23, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Diversified's Yelenick 2 plugged well site located in Nicholson Township, Fayette County following IR 4033716, where a Well Site Restoration Report (WSRR) was denied and violations were issued for failure to restore the well site within 9 months of plugging. A Consent Order and Agreement (COA) with the Department was entered into on 3/07/2019. According to the COA, the Operator shall restore the site within 9 months of plugging. According to Department records, this well was plugged on 10/24/2024, therefore the site shall be fully restored by 7/24/2025 in accordance with current regulations.To date, the Department has yet to receive a WSRR resubmission.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a mailbox and locked gate at the plugged well site's access road entrance. In the on-site mailbox, the Department observed a Post-Plugging Site Restoration Plan. The beginning portion of the access road was observed to be graveled, however the remaining portion of the access road was observed to be restored and exhibiting at least 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth.Upon inspection of the plugged well site, the Department observed the section of the well site where the access road meets the site to still not be exhibiting at least 70% vegetative growth. Seed and mulch was observed to be spread in this location. The rest of the plugged well site appeared to be exhibiting 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. Compost Filter Sock was still observed to be installed downslope of the plugged gas well site.At the time of this inspection no surface fluid leaks or fluid discharges was observed to be coming from the pipeline riser or the approximate coordinate location of the plugged well (According to the Operator NOV response documented in IR 4048289, the pipeline riser is still in use). Based on today's inspection, it appears that the well site and access road is still not fully restored, therefore violations are being continued for failure to restore the well site and access road within 9 months of plugging.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8198629
Permit API: 015-23853
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Rome Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/21/2024
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Chesapeake Appalachia's Crain well site located in Rome Township, Bradford County on 8/21/2024 at 1425 hours. The weather was 63 degrees F with partly cloudy skies. An Act 9 sign remains in place at the site entrance.During my inspection, I discovered elevated electrical conductivity (EC) fluids located outside of the secondary containment structure beneath the produced water tanks. Pooled fluids on the pad surface located behind the produced water tanks (photos #5 and 6) that were field measured for EC ranged from 3.3 to 15.5mS/cm. Pooled fluids on the pad surface located in front of the produced water tanks (photos #7, 8 and 9) ranged from 7.2 to >19.99mS/cm (Over Range). Fluid held within the secondary containment shown in photo #7, beneath the produced water tanks was field measured at >19.99mS/cm.I collected a sample for standard analysis code 942 from the pooled fluids located on the pad surface in front of the produced water tanks (photos #9 and 10). The fluid from where the sample was collected was field measured for EC at >19.99mS/cm. My findings were reported to an environmental representative with Chesapeake via phone shortly after the inspection. The Chesapeake representative stated that a water truck would be dispatched immediately to start recovering the elevated EC fluids discovered. Due to the findings of this inspection report and the elevated EC fluids discovered outside of secondary containment, a violation of CSL 402(b) is cited against API # 015-23853 at this time. Additional violations may be cited based on the results of sample #0983-461. I departed the site at 1510 hours. When I left, heavy rain started to fall.

Matthew Anderson/Big Dog Energy is reportedly the agent intending to operate the gas wells on the Cowden 16 well pad. Both on-site mailboxes which were attached to the Act 9 sign were observed to be empty at the time of this inspection. While on-site, the Department spoke with BDE representatives Matt Kuhn and Chris McNichols, who both were unaware of when the ERP would be available on site. Mr. McNichols prompted Mr. Kuhn call and inquire about the status of the ERP, however, the Department was not made aware of any potential updates regarding the ERP while on-site. Violations are being continued at this time for failure to have the ERP on site.At the time of this inspection, it does not appear that any of the wells at the Cowden well site are in production yet (the 6H, 10H, and 16H). At the time of this inspection, the Department observed a white above ground storage tank on the graveled well pad, the Department did not observe this tank to be connected to gas wells or any other production equipment on the Cowden 16 well pad. Reportedly, this tank is just being stored on the Cowden 16 pad until it could be moved to a different well pad for production use, however, a timeline of when this tank will be removed from the site has yet to be provided to the Department.At the time of this inspection, the Department also observed additional production equipment that did not appear to be connected to any other production equipment or any wells on the well pad. A white structure that was previously observed to be located on site and not connected to any production equipment or wells on the well pad appears to be removed. Violations issued for failure to remove equipment, tanks, and structures not necessary for the production of the well(s) on the Cowden 16 well pad are continued at this time as the white structure was the only equipment not in use observed to be removed from the site at this time.On 4/02/2026, the Department received an email from Mr. Anderson, which states "As we stated our ERPs and some signage was stolen We are having new ones written up and sign ordered. The unused equipment will be in use soon."At the time of this inspection, the DEP observed a well tag fixed to the 6H gas well with all required information posted on it. No fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed to be coming from or near the surface of the 6H gas well at this time.Based on today's inspection, violations issued to the 6H gas well are to remain outstanding at this time.

Report Details

Violation Code: SWMA 302(A) - DISPOSAL, PROCESSING AND STORAGE OF RESIDUAL WASTE - Person disposed, processed, stored, or permitted the disposal, processing or storage of residual waste in a manner which is contrary to the rules and regulations of DEP or to any permit or to the terms or conditions of any permit or any order issued by DEP.
Violation ID: 854469
Permit API: 053-27204
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Jenks Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-06-26
Comments: Site of oil release reported on 6/21/2019 was on a tank battery located east off Salmon Road in a forested area. Oil was released from a hole in the bottom of one of the tanks located in a plastic lined secondary containment. An estimated several barrels of oil were released into the secondary containment. The valved discharge pipe through the secondary containment embankment was open for an unknown period of time after the tank was breached allowing the flow of an estimated one barrel of oil to be released to the ditch north of the tank battery. The oil released into the ditch flowed 10-15 feet in the ditch along the access road until it reached the culvert pipe under the access road, it then flowed through the culvert pipe under the road and continued to 300-400 feet through vegetation down grade from the tank battery. A backhoe was brought in at some point after the oil release and a ditch was dug approximately 70-80 feet down grade of the tank battery to contain the oil release. A second ditch was dug approximately 275 feet north and down grade of the first ditch to contain the oil flow already beyond the first ditch. Absorbent pads and loose absorbents were used to collect oil from the atop the water collected in the ditches. The second ditch/trap was set up with drains to allow water to siphon off leaving the oil in containment. Some oil residue was found on the vegetation east of the lower ditch in a connected depression and in the vegetation 10-20 feet north of the ditch/trap. There was no evidence of oil residue beyond these two areas. The oil and water remaining in the secondary containment was removed by a vacuum tanker truck via the discharge pipe, the remaining oil was removed from the leaking tank as well as from the the other tanks on site on Friday, June 21. There were several precipitation events after the oil was released to ground, one on Friday June 21st, the day of the event, another on Monday June 24, the runoff from these events carried the oil down grade to the above mentioned areas. You are hereby requested to follow Department Policy 550-5000-001, Addressing Spills and Releases at Oil &Gas Well Sites or Access Road. This Policy sets forth the procedures that should be followed to resolve the violations associated with the spill/discharge/release noted in this Notice of Violation by using either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. A copy of the Policy is attached for your review.

The outstanding violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has be confirmed.The DEP recommends:1. Violation ID: 8168601
Permit API: 059-24992
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Morris Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/15/2023
Comments: On December 15, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the WL Hopkins Well Site. The inspection was conducted in response to a request made by an PA DEP OGI during an inspection conducted on 12/15/2023 (Sub-SAIR# 3660126). At the time of inspection, the following was observed:Act 9 Sign Installed, however the Operator of Record does not appear to be correct. The associated PPC plan and ER plan on site have not been updated to reflect the change in ownership. (Photo 11 and 12)The COASTAL Drill Rig was on site and connected to the well. The drill rig and associated equipment was not placed within secondary containment. (Photo 1)I observed fluid on the well pad surrounding the WL Hopkins 590312 Well and drill rig. I also observed fluid within the well cellar. I collected conductivity readings of the fluid on the well pad and within the cellar, which result in elevated conductivity readings. I also observed what appeared to be a light colored crystallin substance deposited on the well pad rock adjacent to the standing fluid. The crystallin substance appears to be salt which suggest that the fluid has been on site long enough to begin evaporation. The amount of fluid on the well pad appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. At the time of inspection, the Department was not previously notified by the Operator of a release of fluid to the well pad. (Photo 2 thru 10)While I was on site, I contacted Operator representative Kevin Wright (CONSOL/Leatherwood) to relay my observations related to the fluid release and recommend that the Operator being remediation immediately. Mr. Wright indicated that the Operator added brine to the well to kill the well on 11/15/2023.I am requesting clarification of the activity, date and time of when the fluid was added to the well bore and all information/inspections related to the monitoring of the well between 11/15/2023 and 12/15/2023. I am also requesting clarification of the source of the fluid added to the well bore on or around 11/15/2023.Violation are being issued for the release (78a.54, 78a57(a), 91.34(a), SWMA 301, 78a66(b)1,78a(b)1(i), 78a66(b)1(ii), 78a66(b)(2), 91.33(a) and 91.33(b).Violations are being issued for the failure to develop a site specific PPC plan and ER Plan. 78a55(a), 78a55(b), 78a55(c). 78a55(h).Violations are being issued for the failure to properly update the Act 9 Sign (78a55(i)(4)(D)(III).Violations are being issued for the failure to install secondary containment. (78a64(a))

Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 12/12/2023
Violation Code: 78.73(a) - GENERAL PROVISION FOR WELL CONSTRUCTION AND OPERATION - Operator failed to construct and operate the well in accordance with 25 Pa. Code Chapter 78 and ensure that the integrity of the well is maintained and health, safety, environment and property are protected.
Violation ID: 8168162
Permit API: 051-23366
Unconventional: No
County: Fayette
Municipality: Georges Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2023
Comments: An onsite inspection of the Kennedy 4 well was conducted by OGI Pat Hiles. Present during the inspection was Diversified representative Gary Molek and Moody and Associates, Inc. representative Jon Hafer. The Department screened around the 7" casing upon arrival with a Bascom Turner 611. Gas readings of 19%, 6%, and 32% gas was detected at various points surrounding the casing. After further investigation, it appeared that Diversified had poured cement around the exposed 7" casing. Placing cement around the casing does not meet repair standards of 78.86. Once Mr. Molek and Mr. Hafer arrived on location, a commingle pressure of the production casing, tubing, and annulus was garnered using a digital pressure gauge. The commingle pressure recorded was 0.6 psi and this location was used as a sample point by Moody. The wellhead was then reconfigured to conduct an annulus shut in test. At 11:51 the annulus pressure was 0.5 psi before blowing the well down. At 11:55 the annulus pressure was 0.9 psi and the casing blown down. At 12:40 the annulus was at 2.0 psi and blown down to collect a sample. Although pressure was relatively low, there was decent volume. The area surrounding the wellhead was screened for soil gas at intervals of 2 ft, 10 ft, and 20 ft. Soil gas readings from Moody and the Department will be listed below. Landowner has a water well approximately 200 ft from the wellhead. The landowner stated his water well is drilled to a depth of 200 ft. Landowner's water was field screened by Moody and the results were 2% LEL, 2880 ppm, and 5220 ppm. The landowner's basement headspace and water well connections were also screened by Moody with no gas readings detected. Person stored, transported, processed, or disposed of residual waste inconsistent with or unauthorized by the rules and regulations of DEP.
Violation ID: 8268741
Permit API: 059-26446
Unconventional: Yes
County: Greene
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/27/2026
Comments: On 03/27/2026, an incident inspection was conducted at the Anthony Petraitis Well Site following receipt of a spill report, submitted to the Department on 03/26/2026 (CTS 396174). I was accompanied by Water Quality Specialist Laura Grada (PA DEP), EQT representative Doug Oberdorf, and SPSI representative Billy Wade. SPSI was on site for remediation.EQT reported a spill of approximately 5 gallons of production fluid from a flow line. They reported that SPSI was on site, the release was contained, and no waterways were affected.EQT indicated on site that they intend to remediate per Act 2 guidelines. The fluid was on the pad, underneath the pad liner; the pad liner was above the pad substrate and contained pea gravel overtop of the liner. When the Department arrived on site, SPSI indicated that 1 vac box was around half full of the removed fluids; this was the only box that was used, and none were removed from site full.The following was observed during inspection:SPSI had vac trucks on site and were in the process of remediation (Photo 1).The spill was located around Gas Production Unit (GPU) 6H. The leak originated at the elbow joint of the associated GPU piping. The spilled fluid reached the underside of the pad liner; the fluid was also pooling on top of the pad liner, within the pea gravel (Photos 2-5).Several sumps were dug on both sides of the spill origin at GPU 6H and its associated elbow joint within the piping. Conductivity readings were obtained within the soil and water at the sump locations. The sump located 15 feet from the elbow joint yielded a conductivity reading of 1835 uS/cm within the soil (Photo 6). The sump 30 feet from the elbow joint yielded a conductivity reading of 644 uS/cm within the soil (Photo 7). The sump located 10 feet from the elbow yielded a water conductivity reading of 13.04 mS/cm and a soil reading of 6.18 mS/cm (Photos 8, 9). The sump located 35 feet from the elbow yielded a conductivity reading of 2.86 mS/cm within the soil this reading was unable to be replicated; the operator will monitor this location (Photo 10). Permit API: 065-26269
Unconventional: No

Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3788146), I noted API 065-26269 did not have a well tag, equipment not necessary for production was being stored on site, and there was evidence of a production fluid release greater than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection (FUI) on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790440), I noted the well had a new well tag, the pipe was moved across the access road, and the spill area was seeded and mulched. The Department did not receive a response from the Notice of Violation with the operators intentions to use either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from the spill. The tag violation was closed. The other violations remained open.On a FUI on 8/19/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3816085), I noted the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts or waste manifests regarding the clean up of this site. I emailed Ray Hepler information about Act 2 remediation. On 8/28/2024, Jack Crow, Henry Kramer, Brian Shank and myself met with Ray Hepler at the PA DEP Meadville Regional Office to discuss the outstanding violations at the Wheeler property. Ray Hepler stated he had the contaminated soil from the brine releases on a roll off and would send us the manifests soon. The Department received a manifest for waste on 9/9/2024. However, the manifest stated the soil was "Beaver-PA 100%". The manifest also stated the soil was hauled in a "white pick up truck", but during the 8/28/2024 meeting Ray Hepler stated the soil was in a roll off container. This manifest does not show the proper disposal of the soil from the Wheeler W12 well site located in Jefferson County. Today (9/12/2024), Brian Shank and I conducted a FUI. The pipe not necessary for production was still being stored near the access road. The spill area appeared to have new top soil and grass seed. We collected soil conductivity readings throughout the spill area. A background soil conductivity reading was collected. The soil conductivity reading was 154.5 pS/cm. Near the production tank, the soil conductivity reading was 3.28 mS/cm. Approximately 4 feet from the production tank, the soil conductivity reading 1416 pS/cm. These readings indicate that the prior spill has not been remediated yet. We collected grab soil samples to send to the Department's accredited laboratory. The samples will be analyzed for SAC 960 and UVIR.The outstanding violations for the Wheeler W12 well site will remain open at this time.

Comments: On March 21, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release.At the time of the inspection the well site appeared unchanged from the Department's previous inspection on 3/20/2025.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. Other production equipment was observed on site and appeared to be charred, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near any of this production equipment. A production tank was observed on site with a large hole in its side, the tank had approximately 1-2 in of fluid pooled at the bottom of it, no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this production tank.A soil conductivity reading was taken directly under the hole in the tank with a reading of 10.16mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. The Department observed 2 booms installed in the ditch. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of 10.43mS, 7.28mS, 1.27mS, 0.93mS, 0.68mS, 0.78mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. Conductivity readings were taken in this area of the ditch with readings of 0.53mS, 0.38mS, and 0.46mS.A conductivity reading was taken upstream of where the ditch appears to terminate with a reading of 0.67mS. A conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.76mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings obtained, it appears that the conductivity readings are comparable to the previous inspections in regards to distance and levels of elevated readings in the ditch. It appears that released fluids may have been contained to the portions of the ditch where standing fluid was observed, and it did not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.Prior to leaving the site, the Department called operator representative Ben Dickun to inquire when remediation was going to begin. Mr. Dickun stated they have contacted their consultant (Moody) and that work to remediate as well as a site assessment/sampling by Moody was scheduled to occur on Tuesday, 3/25/2025. The Department recommended during the call that immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

Mr. Dickun stated they have contacted their consultant (Moody) and that work to remediate as well as a site assessment/sampling by Moody was scheduled to occur on Tuesday, 3/25/2025. The Department recommended during the call that immediate measures are properly implemented to commence remediation in response to the brine release that occurred onsite during the 3/19/2025 incident to prevent further migration of the onsite pollution and prevent pollution into WOC.Based on today's inspection, violations issued during IR 3941481 and 3941519 shall remain outstanding.

Permit API: 033-26887
Unconventional: Yes
County: Clearfield
Municipality: Lawrence Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2019-10-11
Comments: Doug Kepler of Seneca Resources called and reported a mixed brine/water spill of 1 barrel to the Department on October 10, 2019 at 1600. Mr. Kepler stated that crews were onsite cleaning up the spill as he was reporting it to the Department. Chapter 78a.66(b)2 states that all spills and/or releases should be reported to the Department within 2 hours after detecting or discovery of the release. I conducted an incident site inspection on October 11, 2019 with Kyle Kline of Seneca Resources at D-17 COP-B well pad. According to Mr. Kline, a well tender was onsite the previous day plunging well (033-26887) when a float got stuck on the separator. Pressure built up over time causing fluids to be released through the rupture disc located on the GPU separator. During my inspection I viewed the separator, the impacted area adjacent to the seperator, and the roll off box containing the impacted materials. I conducted field screenings using a soil probe randomly throughout the excavated area. Screenings ranged from 0 uS/cm- 220 uS/cm. Approximately 2-3 cubic yards of impacted materials were viewed inside the lined roll-off box. Please note, that Seneca Resources sent the Department an email on October 15, 2015 revising the initial spill volume from 1 barrel to 0.5-0.75 barrels of produced fluids released. This information was revised based off the well tenders report of claiming that the plunger system brings 1-1.5 barrels of produced fluids with each cycle. According to the well tender about 50% of the fluids went to the tank and the other 50% was released to the pads surface. Based off the Departments inspection, the Department concurs with this spill volume correction. Violations have been noted and have been immediately corrected.

The fluid escaping from the valve is recommended to be addressed. A reading was obtained within the gravel around the pan of Tank 4. This reading was 4.28 mS (Photo 3).Readings were taken within the gravel in the battery around Tank 5 and within the fluid in the pan. The readings within the gravel were 4.76 mS and 4.26 mS (Photos 4, 5). The reading within the pan was 17.30 mS (Photos 6, 7), which may indicate fluids leaking from tank fluid removal or from the valve itself. I recommend that this is addressed. I recommend that additional is added as needed (Photos 10, 11).Pans are under each tank valve (Photo 12).Wet spots were noted on the exterior of the earthen berm. Conductivity readings were taken within these noted areas and resulted in the following: 4.00 mS, 6.33 mS, 5.44 mS. Another reading resulted in 1.15 mS. I recommend that fluid from inside the battery is not migrate through the berm. Livestock activity in the vicinity is taken into consideration (Photos 13-17). The violations issued on 12/29/2023 and 01/31/2024 remain outstanding.

Comments: On October 17 2025 the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Gaut 4 Well Pad in regards to a spill reported to the Department at 9:23am on 10/17/2025 (CTS 393035). Present during the inspection was operator representative Bruce Carpenter.The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that appeared to have all required information. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel, with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site appeared to exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.During the inspection, Mr. Carpenter showed the Department the location of the spill. According to Mr. Carpenter, the spill occurred around 8:00am on 10/17/2025. The spill of approximately 10 gallons of production fluid occurred from a flow line that ran from the wellhead to a gas buster unit. Upon observation of the spill the flow to the line was stopped. Mr. Carpenter stated that clean up crews were on route to remediate the spill. He stated that the gas buster and the secondary containment would be moved so all contaminated material could be removed. He stated that when reconnected, the gas buster and entire flowline would be in secondary containment to ensure another spill does not occur. He also stated that a valve would be added to the flow line so a pressure test could be conducted prior to using the line again.At the time of the inspection, the Department observed the location of the spill adjacent to the gas buster, below the flow line. Saturated/stained gravel was observed in this area. The spill appeared to be approximately 15 feet long by 10 feet wide. It appeared the contaminated area extended under the secondary containment for the gas buster unit. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of the saturated/stained gravel with readings of 17.97mS, 17.50mS, and 5.60mS. It appeared the conductivity readings decreased with distance away from the flow line. A reading was taken just outside the saturated/stained gravel with a reading of 0.04mS. A background conductivity reading was taken away from the location of the spill with a reading of 0.05mS.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Upon inspection of the additional production equipment onsite, the production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks. There were no visible leaks with the GPU, and it appeared not to be in secondary containment, however the well was drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a.OGI referral is being requested to follow up on current onsite operations. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

Violation ID: 8253091
Permit API: 129-28877
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Washington Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 10/17/2025
Comments: On October 17 2025 the Department conducted an incident inspection at the Gaut 4 Well Pad in regards to a spill reported to the Department at 9:23am on 10/17/2025 (CTS 393035). Present during the inspection was operator representative Bruce Carpenter.The findings are as follows: At the time of the inspections, the Act 9 sign was present and appeared to be properly installed. The Department observed an Emergency Response Plan and a Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan that appeared to have all required information. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel, with no erosion or sedimentation issues observed. The well site appeared to exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation issues were observed.During the inspection, Mr. Carpenter showed the Department the location of the spill. According to Mr. Carpenter, the spill occurred around 8:00am on 10/17/2025. The spill of approximately 10 gallons of production fluid occurred from a flow line that ran from the wellhead to a gas buster unit. Upon observation of the spill the flow to the line was stopped. Mr. Carpenter stated that clean up crews were on route to remediate the spill. He stated that the gas buster and the secondary containment would be moved so all contaminated material could be removed. He stated that when reconnected, the gas buster and entire flowline would be in secondary containment to ensure another spill does not occur. He also stated that a valve would be added to the flow line so a pressure test could be conducted prior to using the line again.At the time of the inspection, the Department observed the location of the spill adjacent to the gas buster, below the flow line. Saturated/stained gravel was observed in this area. The spill appeared to be approximately 15 feet long by 10 feet wide. It appeared the contaminated area extended under the secondary containment for the gas buster unit. Conductivity readings were taken in the area of the saturated/stained gravel with readings of 17.97mS, 17.50mS, and 5.60mS. It appeared the conductivity readings decreased with distance away from the flow line. A reading was taken just outside the saturated/stained gravel with a reading of 0.04mS. A background conductivity reading was taken away from the location of the spill with a reading of 0.05mS.The operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. The Department also requests the waste manifest from the site remediation be submitted upon receipt.Upon inspection of the additional production equipment onsite, the production tanks appeared to be within secondary containment and appeared sound with no visible fluid leaks. There were no visible leaks with the GPU, and it appeared not to be in secondary containment, however the well was drilled prior to the promulgation of 78a.OGI referral is being requested to follow up on current onsite operations. Based on today's inspection, violations are being issued for the observed release.

I also observed a puddle of an oily substance with a green tint in the travel lane along the southern side of the pad. Company man Yadir Lozano said that this had been found just prior to my arrival on location and that they would excavate the impacted gravel material right away. Comments: On May 15, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3944466, where violations were left outstanding due to no Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3944466, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (see photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack secondary containment, as is required at unconventional well sites (see photos 2-5). The top hatch of the production tank closest to the well head was not observed on the ground during this inspection. The Department recommended in IR 3944466 that this top hatch be replaced onto the production tank to prevent possible overflowing with rainwater.The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (see photos 1 and 4). The access road remains stabilized with gravel. The well tag that was affixed to the well head during the time of IR 3944466 appears to have been removed. No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 6). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (see photo 7). The Department recommends that equipment onsite that is not in use for production is removed from site. The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (see photos 8 and 9).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued from IR 3944466 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Comments: On August 19, 2024 the Department (DEP) conducted a follow up inspection of State Game Lands 51B1 Well located in Dunbar Township, Fayette County, where violations were continued for a release from production equipment inside the green shed.At the time of this inspection, Minor rutting is developing in the access road as it enters the well site; therefore, the Department recommends the operator continue to monitor and maintain the access road as necessary in order to prevent any erosion and sedimentation events from occurring. The well site is exhibiting greater than 70% uniformand adequate vegetative growth with the exception of the area where a production tank had previously been placed. The DEP recommends this area be seeded and mulched. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues were observed during this inspection.Two production tanks within secondary containment were observed. One of the production tanks appeared rusted but no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed. However, the tank's secondary containment was nearly full of fluid. The DEP recommends that the containment be drained, fluid be disposed of properly, and in accordance with regulations. The well tag was present at the time of this inspection. A well tag was found on the ground near wellhead. The Dept recommends the Operator permanently affix the well tag in accordance with 3211(h) . There were no observed leaks or discharge on the ground or around the wellhead. No fluid discharges were observed coming from the production tank near the wellhead onsite, however, the production tanks lid was cracked in half and open and there appeared to be a high level of fluid in this production tank. The DEP recommends the Operator replace the lid on this production tank and properly dispose of the contents within this tank to prevent a potential release. The production tank near the green shed had a hose inside the secondary containment extending out onto the ground. It appears that water in the secondary containment is being discharged to the ground as the secondary containment is at capacity. The Department recommends the removal of this excess fluid in accordance with current regulations to accommodate any potential releases that may occur. Inside the green shed located on this well site, a compressor station as well as various barrels with various unknown substances not in containment were observed. Some barrels were heavily rusted and staining in the gravel was observed underneath them as well as under the GPU and production equipment. The Department request the Operator provide information on what exactly is in the drums and what they are being used for. The Department request that this information be provided with the NOV response. The Department also recommends that the Operator remove all equipment/supplies not necessary for production.Inside the green shed, the spill that was previously observed in inspection reports 3743832 and 3808945 remains. In this green shed, the spill appears to be an oily like petroleum substance on the ground. The DEP again recommends that the Operator remediate the areas as necessary in accordance with the Department's Spill Policy. The DEP again requests the operator evaluate the releases that have occurred and provide a quantity of what was released, what specific fluids were released, and when and how the release occurred. The GPU unit (not in secondary containment) in this green shed had no observable active leaks or discharge.Based on today's inspection violations for the spill shall remain outstanding along with failure to have the well tag permanently affixed to the wellhead.
